messages.text: I need help with return RMA.

I'm Hal, HeliumDeploy's technical specialist, and I'll help you get this sorted.

First I need to check what's wrong with the unit. Please tell me:

1. Which miner it is (for example NerdQX, Bitaxe, Hammer DC06) and which order it came on, if you have more than one.
2. What it's doing: no power at all, no hashing, an error on the screen, physical damage, or something else.

If there's an error message on the screen or in the web page, a photo or screenshot of it helps a lot.

Thanks, a GekkoAxe V2.

What's it doing wrong? For example:

- no power, nothing lights up
- it powers on but isn't hashing, or the hashrate is low
- there's an error on the screen or in the web page
- something is physically damaged, like the screen or the fan

If there's an error message, a photo or screenshot of it is the quickest way for me to tell what's going on.
When power on giving Hardware Problem. Board Initialization Failed
Searched the web · "Board Initialization Failed" bitaxe AxeOS hardware problem
Searched the web · ESP-Miner "Board Initialization Failed"
Searched the web · GekkoScience GekkoAxe V2 "Hardware Problem" board initializa
Searched the web · bitaxe screen "Hardware Problem" ASIC init failed power

I looked up that exact message for the GekkoAxe V2 and couldn't find an official explanation from the maker, so I won't guess at it. Generally it means the board couldn't start the mining chip. That can come from the power supply or from the board itself, and I'll check the power first.

Please send me:

1. **A photo of the screen** showing the error. If the version number shows when it boots, include that too.
2. **The power supply you're using**: is it the one that came in the box? What do its label's volts and amps say?
3. **Have you tried a different power supply** that matches those volts and amps? If yes, did the error stay the same?
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)
Searched the web · GekkoScience GekkoAxe firmware ESP-Miner github

Thanks for the screenshot, it helps a lot. It's the miner's firmware page, and it says **"Running 0.2101 on bitaxe-gamma-601 (ota_0)"** and "Firmware is up to date".

The firmware is set up for a **standard Bitaxe Gamma 601**, not a GekkoAxe. That could be the problem. GekkoAxe boards use their own power settings. Firmware built for GekkoAxe has 
dedicated device family entries for each board variant (GekkoAxe-GT, GekkoAxe-γ) with correct regulator config, fan controller, and board-specific power parameters
, and the GekkoAxe Gamma 12V has its own board ID (
gekko-601-12
). If the board is running settings meant for a different board, the power regulator may refuse to start the chip. That would show up as "Board Initialization Failed" without anything being broken.

Before anything else, please try this and tell me what happens:

1. Unplug the power cable from the miner completely and wait 30 seconds. Restarting from the web page isn't enough.
2. Plug it back in and watch the screen. Does "Board Initialization Failed" come back?

Please also tell me:
- **Did the miner arrive with this firmware, or did you install or update it yourself?**
- **What does the power supply label say** for volts and amps, and is it the one that came in the box?

Please don't flash any other firmware yet. Once I know where this version came from, I'll point you to the right firmware for your exact board.
Using Power supply that came with unit. Check voltage with meter 12 volts DC Good.

That rules out a dead power supply. Thanks for checking it with a meter.

Your 12 V reading also fits what I said about the firmware. The Bitaxe Gamma 601 is a **5 V** board. GekkoAxe firmware lets each board set its own 
TPS546 input voltage thresholds
 (the power regulator's limits for the voltage coming in), using 
vin_on, vin_off, and vin_ov_fault
 settings. If the miner thinks it's a 5 V Gamma 601 and gets 12 V, the regulator may treat that as too much voltage and refuse to start the chip. You'd see exactly "Board Initialization Failed" even though the board is fine. I can't confirm that's the cause from here yet, but it's the most likely one.

Two quick things so I can point you to the right firmware:

1. **Did the unplug test change anything?** That's the 30 seconds fully unplugged, then plugged back in.
2. **Where did this firmware come from?** Did the miner arrive with it, or did you install or update it yourself? Do you remember roughly when the error started, for example right after an update?

Please don't flash anything yet. If the wrong file goes on, it can make things harder to recover.
I am not sure what Firmware came on the unit. I installed update when it would gave the fault out of the box.
Handed to the team · Probable wrong board profile and TPS546 VIN limits: the unit gets 12 V input but

I've sent the details of your GekkoAxe V2 to JD, our hardware lead. The team picks it up today at 10am ET, and the answer will come to your email.

So far: the error showed up straight out of the box, your power supply measures a healthy 12 V, and the firmware is set up for a 5 V Bitaxe Gamma 601 instead of a GekkoAxe. Your update kept that same board setting, which is why it didn't help. Fixing it most likely means a full reinstall with the right GekkoAxe V2 firmware and settings over USB. I don't want to guess at the file, because the wrong one can make things worse, so JD will confirm the exact one.

If you'd like a faster answer, join our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and mention **@nullhashrate** (that's JD). He and the community are very active there.

One small thing will help him: did unplugging it for 30 seconds and plugging it back in change anything, or does it still show "Board Initialization Failed"?
